comparator.name: Nutrition and Health
comparator.sourceNotes: Current2026–2027 BVG handbook:121EC compulsory common courses,3EC prior-mathematics-dependent choice and12EC literature thesis establish136EC of common study; this example uses44EC genuine electives to total180. The zero-to-four-credit optional skills group and6EC same-group laboratory thesis extension are not selected. All57B1 common credits plus3EC mathematics are completed; all60B2 compulsory credits and Skills Development Part1 precede thesis entry, exceeding the102compulsory-credit threshold. Part3 portfolio is completed with electives/thesis, not falsely required before it. General/laboratory safety are additional zero-credit requirements. No formal specialisation/minor instantiated; current module requirements and assessments control, not historical course guides.

components.name: Nutrition and Health: Macronutrients, Energy and Health
components.note: Both study carbohydrates, fats, proteins, enzymes and energy metabolism. WUR adds dedicated nutrition, body-weight regulation and the health effects of particular macronutrients.

components.name: Introduction to the Field of Nutrition and Health
Basic Skills for BVG-students
components.note: WUR combines information-literacy training with Excel. UCR’s PPD shares scholarly searching and source evaluation, while adding writing, reflection and civic engagement; it does not reproduce the Excel module. General and laboratory safety are additional zero-credit requirements; laboratory safety must precede the practicals.

components.name: Statistics 2
components.note: Both courses teach estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing. WUR also develops simple regression for life-science data; UCR’s Probability & Statistics has a more mathematical and computational emphasis.

components.name: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
components.note: Shared chemical equilibria, thermodynamic and quantitative physical-chemical tools provide a partial relationship. UCR’s course uses sustainability and materials examples, rather than a full life-science chemistry sequence.

components.name: Microbiology for Nutrition and Health
components.note: The shared microbiological methods include bacterial culture, identification and experimental analysis. WUR additionally studies microbial diversity and gastrointestinal microbiota; UCR’s laboratory course also covers blood, proteins and DNA.

components.name: Introduction to Epidemiology and Public Health
Measuring Dietary Intake
components.note: WUR teaches dietary-assessment instruments, reference values, biomarkers and measurement error. General interviewing or data analysis is not a substitute for this specialist training.

components.name: Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms for Health
Research Methodology for Nutrition and Health I
components.note: The shared research-design methods include questions, measurement, sampling, experimental planning and ethics. WUR applies these to nutritional protocols, including participant allocation, blinding and compliance.

components.name: Research Methodology for Nutrition and Health II
components.note: WUR students conduct a dietary intervention and measurements such as body composition, energy expenditure, biomarkers and sensory analysis. The selected UCR courses do not reproduce this integrated nutritional practical.

components.name: Skills Development for BVG-Part 1
components.note: Skills development is an integrated portfolio of presenting, writing, collaboration and supporting skills. Part 1 must be completed before the thesis.

components.name: Skills Development for BVG-Part 3
components.note: Part 3 develops and records presenting and writing through electives and the thesis. Its 1 EC is separate from the 12 EC thesis, rather than a duplicate thesis award.

components.name: Mathematics Applied: Introduction
components.note: This example uses Mathematics Applied: Introduction for students with VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; the choice is determined by prior preparation.

components.name: BSc Thesis Nutrition and Health
components.note: The required 12 EC thesis is an individual literature study with a research proposal, report, presentation and final discussion. Entry requires at least 102 credits of compulsory first- and second-year study, all first-year courses and Skills Development Part 1. The optional 6 EC laboratory extension is not selected here.

components.name: Open electives
components.note: This example retains 44 EC for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. Selecting optional skills courses or the laboratory thesis extension can reduce that space; neither is added here.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Current formal prerequisites precede every dependent course; every assigned term is planned. Gateways precede disciplinary study, Cell Biology precedes Pathology/Genetics, physiology precedes pharmacology, basic empirical design precedes research synthesis/advanced analysis, programming precedes ML and introductory sociology precedes modern sociology. These improvements do not create extra hard prerequisites.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Shared cellular organisation, membranes, signalling, gene regulation and molecular methods; biological examples and practical scope differ.
Shared normal organ-system physiology, homeostasis, digestive/endocrine and energy regulation. WUR adds its own physiology practicals.

Shared carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, enzyme processes and energy metabolism are important primary content. WUR additionally develops macronutrient-specific nutrition/health effects and body-weight regulation.

Shared experimental microbial culture/identification, basic microbiology and biochemical/molecular laboratory reasoning. WUR additionally emphasises microbial diversity and gastrointestinal microbiota.
Shared inheritance, genetic variation, epigenetics, disease mechanisms and genetic technologies. WUR includes its own human-genetics wet-lab genotype/phenotype work.
Shared drug action, kinetics, metabolism and dose-response foundations. WUR additionally examines dietary bioactives, supplements and nutrient–drug interactions.
Shared innate/adaptive immunity, immune-cell mechanisms, immune disorders and laboratory-data analysis; WUR additionally examines nutritional immunomodulation.
Shared chemical equilibria, thermodynamic/energy and quantitative physical-chemical tools; UCR’s environmental/material contexts differ from the focused life-science chemistry course.
No adequate whole counterpart for organic reaction mechanisms, stereochemistry and natural-product chemistry; general biochemical/sustainability contributions remain bounded.
Distinct nutrition-specific orientation, longitudinal skills or assessment requirement is not equated with a generic method or broad introductory course.
Additional dedicated micronutrient/energy nutrition remains separate; the strongest biochemical macronutrient course is aligned to Macronutrients, Energy and Health.
No selected course directly implements food processing/storage effects on nutrient function/digestibility and food labelling/legislation.
Additional integrated normal physiological regulation/inter-organ training remains separate; the strongest shared physiological course is already aligned to Principles of Human Physiology.
Clinical disease mechanisms are not a substitute for toxicological exposure, organ-specific toxicity and risk assessment.
Dietary instruments, reference intakes, biomarkers and intake measurement error are not replaced by generic qualitative interviewing or data cleaning.
Additional human infectious-disease content remains separate; the strongest host-defence course is aligned to Human Immunology.
The integrated human dietary-intervention and nutritional-measurement practical is not reproduced by general laboratory or statistical training.
Shared epidemiological measures, designs, bias/confounding and population-health reasoning; UCR also develops intervention/stakeholder appraisal.
Shared social cognition, influence, group behaviour and theory-guided social-psychological research.
Shared biopsychosocial determinants of behaviour, health inequalities and prevention/behaviour-change frameworks. WUR focuses on eating patterns and nutritional behaviour.
Shared practical speech organisation, rhetorical choices, delivery and public presentation; UCR adds argumentation/storytelling and WUR targets scientific presentations.
No selected course implements food taste/smell panels, hedonic/analytical measures and food-product sensory profiling.
Shared scholarly information searching, evaluation and academic research literacy. WUR additionally requires Excel; UCR adds writing, reflection and civic engagement.

Shared research-question/design, measurement, sampling, experimental logic, ethics and empirical project planning. WUR’s protocols are specifically nutritional, including blinding, allocation, compliance and participant measures.
Shared multivariable regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures designs, assumptions and R-based data interpretation.
Shared structured programming/problem solving, data collections and algorithmic implementation. WUR explicitly frames data structures and algorithms through health problems.
Shared functions, differentiation/integration and quantitative problem-solving support the selected conditional mathematics component. UCR extends into dynamic models and differential equations.
Shared probability-based estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests. WUR develops simple applied regression; UCR emphasises mathematical inference and simulation.

Shared critical literature searching, evidence selection/appraisal and analytical synthesis/reporting give a specific research-method relationship. UCR has a taught team meta-analysis, while WUR requires an individual supervised12EC literature thesis with proposal, report, presentation and defence. Optional UCR research remains an additional opportunity.

The required 12 EC thesis is an individual literature study with a research proposal, report, presentation and final discussion. Entry requires at least 102 credits of compulsory first- and second-year study, all first-year courses and Skills Development Part 1. The optional 6 EC laboratory extension is not selected here.
Skills development is an integrated portfolio of presenting, writing, collaboration and supporting skills. Part 1 must be completed before the thesis.
Part 3 develops and records presenting and writing through electives and the thesis. Its 1 EC is separate from the 12 EC thesis, rather than a duplicate thesis award.
This example retains 44 EC for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. Selecting optional skills courses or the laboratory thesis extension can reduce that space; neither is added here.

notes.text: WUR provides a dedicated nutrition sequence in macro- and micronutrients, food technology, dietary-intake measurement, food sensory science and human nutritional interventions. UCR can combine substantial biomedical mechanisms, physiology, epidemiology, health behaviour and research methods, but these related programmes do not reproduce that specialist sequence. WUR’s 12 EC individual thesis is required; UCR’s optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: WUR’s Dutch-taught Nutrition and Health bachelor studies how diet and lifestyle affect human health, from molecules and organs to behaviour and populations. It combines biomedical science with nutritional assessment, food and sensory science, experiments and independent research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines biological mechanisms with health behaviour and public-health research. The second emphasises molecular and organ mechanisms, laboratory work and research computing; the third emphasises health behaviour, prevention and policy. These are related approaches: WUR offers substantially more dedicated nutritional science, dietary assessment, food technology, sensory testing and human nutrition interventions. Its individual thesis is required; UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits.
